subject: Solarflare capacity contention — urgent allocation decision (SF-477)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Solarflare - urgent dedicated capacity ask for go-live (SF-477)

Team — heads up, Solarflare (Alex Moreno) just notified me that their production rollout on 2026-11-01 needs 64 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for an initial 3-month window. They are asking for guaranteed dedicated capacity (no preemption) and a 95% token SLO for the first 30 days.

Quick context: they signed a term sheet for ~$1.2M ARR (deal SF-477). This is a strategic vertical AI customer — they are pushing for an enterprise SLA and want capacity locked in now. They attached the customer request (solarflare_capacity_request.xlsx).

Key numbers from the ask:
- Dedicated GPUs requested: 64 (A100-equivalent) starting 2026-11-01
- Expected peak QPS: ~1800 requests/minute during peak windows
- Initial commitment: 3 months, with option to extend

I haven’t promised anything yet. Can infra/ops quickly say whether we can: (a) allocate 64 dedicated now, (b) propose a hybrid with guaranteed 32 + 32 burst, or (c) give a firm start date if we need to shuffle other deals.

Alex is CCed on this thread so we can field clarifying Qs. Ben

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-20T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Solarflare - urgent dedicated capacity ask for go-live (SF-477)

Thanks Ben — looping infra and ops formally. Alex / Solarflare: we hear you and will treat this as high priority. Internal owners: please review fleet availability and provide three concrete allocation options (fastest, safest compromise, least customer impact) with pros/cons and rollback criteria.

Requested deliverables by EOD today:
- Vivek: capacity feasibility + impact to named customers (list out which deals would be shifted or preempted)
- Rishi: commercial decision constraints (minimum revenue threshold / SLA concessions we can accept)
- Laura: customer-side expectations and contract levers we can offer to reduce hard capacity needs (e.g., phased ramp, traffic shaping)

Alex, we may propose a short-term compromise while we resolve the full capacity plan. Will keep you posted with options.

— Soojin

Subject: Re: Solarflare - urgent dedicated capacity ask for go-live (SF-477)

Digested the request and checked fleet state. Short answer: we can support the launch, but there are trade-offs. Below are three operational options with impact analysis.

Option A — Compromise (recommended)
- 32 dedicated GPUs reserved + 32 burstable from preemptible pool
- Start date: 2026-11-01 (ready)
- Impact: minimal reshuffle needed; affects queued burst for non-enterprise customers by ~12% during peak; no immediate contract churn anticipated
- Mitigation: apply caching + KV prefixing for Solarflare, encourage model quantization for cost reduction

Option B — Full dedicated 64 (high-assurance)
- 64 dedicated GPUs guaranteed (no preemption)
- Start date: earliest realistic is 2026-11-08 due to current tranche allocations; requires moving two mid-tier reserved lanes (customers: Nimbus, Helios) with outreach + credits
- Impact: medium (customer outreach required, potential churn risk if credits not agreeable)

Option C — Delayed dedicated with traffic shaping
- 16 dedicated + 16 burst now; remaining 32 ramp over 4 weeks after launch
- Start date: 2026-11-01 with phased capacity increases
- Impact: lower immediate fleet disturbance, but Solarflare may be dissatisfied if they see throttling early on

Operational notes:
- Fleet inventory: A100-equivalent free capacity this week = ~48 GPUs (depending on node topology). We can rebench some tranches but that costs time and credits.
- Risk to other customers: Nimbus and Helios are the two most exposed if we do full reassignments.

Attachments: fleet-availability-20261020.pdf (contains per-region node map and scheduling constraints).

My recommendation is Option A as a pragmatic compromise — keeps launch date intact, gives Solarflare meaningful guaranteed capacity, and reduces churn risk. If sales/legal insist on full 64 guaranteed, we need an explicit approval for tranche movement plus a compensation plan.

— Vivek

Alex — appreciate the clarity on timelines. From a CS/contracting perspective the ask for 95% token SLO and 64 non-preemptible GPUs is a high bar. If we deliver Option A (32+32 burst), we should offer a short-term commercial concession to get them comfortable (onboarding credit + a 30-day performance SLA review).

If leadership decides Option B (full 64), legal will want the following changes in the SOW:
- Explicit force-majeure and capacity exception language
- Credit formula for missed SLOs tied to measured token loss

We need a rapid decision window — Solarflare expects an answer by EOD tomorrow. Also, procurement asked for a signed SOW attachment; I uploaded a draft SOW (solarflare_sow_v3.pdf) with placeholder SLA language.

— Laura

Leadership — we need a single decision here. My operational read: Option A (32 dedicated + 32 burstable) is the least risky near-term and allows us to meet 11/01. I’m asking for two approvals by EOD tomorrow:

1) Rishi — authorization to implement Option A and sign off on the compensation/credit package (no more than $45k onboarding credit).
2) Vivek — confirmation you can roll Option A without impacting any existing committed SLAs for current enterprise customers; include rollback steps.

If either of you vetoes, we’ll present Option B as the alternative and include the customer outreach plan. Ben: please coordinate with Alex and procurement so we have a mutual action plan ready.

— Soojin

Approved: Option A (32 dedicated + 32 burstable) with two conditions:
1) Update SOW to reflect that 32 GPUs are guaranteed and 32 are burstable with defined preemption windows; include an explicit monitoring & rollback clause.
2) Sales to include the $45k onboarding credit and commit to a 30-day joint performance review tied to SLA metrics.

Vivek — please proceed with the operational changes and share the exact tranche movements so CS can notify impacted customers. Laura — legal and procurement to add the highlighted language to the SOW and route for signature. Ben — confirm with Alex and get them to sign the revised SOW by 10/25.

I’m OK with this compromise given the strategic upside and the credit buffer. Keep me posted on any downstream churn signals.

— Rishi
